set_description.description: Powers Hapgood was a Harvard-educated coal miner, Socialist and labor organizer, who was arrested and jailed numerous times over his life for his activism. During the Somerset County Pennsylvania coal strike Hapgood was reportedly arrested more than a dozen times for leading marches and entering company-owned mining towns to organize or picket. During the Sacco–Vanzetti trial, he was arrested several times for attempting to speak or organize demonstrations including one arrest where he was committed to the Boston Psychopathic Hospital. Hapgood later became a prominent CIO organizer and served two months in 1937 for leading a Lewiston–Auburn Maine shoe strike in violation of a court injunction banning strike activities.
